tools.ruotaLaScalaInMano: Rotate the stairs in hand (R): changes the side you enter from
tools.eliminaUnClicToglieLa: Delete: a click removes the door or the stairs, dragging draws an area and on release the pieces it touches disappear
tools.scalaSiMettonoACoppie: Stairs: placed in pairs, one click per end; the second is linked to the first
tools.separaUnClicSuUn: Split: a click on an obstacle detaches it from its group (rubble, pits and water); on a pit or water already split it joins it back
tools.eliminaUnClicToglieL: Delete: a click removes the obstacle or the wall, dragging draws an area and on release the pieces it touches disappear

tools.ricompenseDeiBauliLaTabella: Chest rewards: the table of finds

tools.eliminaUnClicToglieL2: Delete: a click removes the item, dragging draws an area and on release the pieces it touches disappear

tools.ruotaIlNemicoInMano: Rotate the enemy in hand (R): changes how its squares are laid out
tools.eliminaUnClicToglieIl2: Delete: a click removes the enemy, dragging draws an area and on release the pieces it touches disappear
tools.eliminaUnClicSuUn: Delete: a click on an area deletes it (the map stays); if it already has texts it asks for confirmation
tools.creaUnAreaToccaI: Create an area: tap the pieces to include, then confirm with the blue check
tools.variabiliDellAvventuraGliInterrutt: Adventure variables: the switches that events turn on and read
tools.eliminaUnClicSuUn2: Delete: a click on an event deletes it (it asks for confirmation)
tools.nessunEventoAncoraPremiPer: No events yet. Press + to create one: "when this happens, if that holds, do this".
infoDialog.ilTestoCheIGiocatori: The text players read before starting.
infoDialog.lIntroduzioneSiScriveIn: The introduction is written in markdown:
goalsDialog.cheCosaDevonoFareGli: What the heroes must do to win.
goalsDialog.regoleCheValgonoSoloIn: Rules that only apply in this adventure: the heroes read them after the objective, at the start of the game.
goalsDialog.ilTestoCheIGiocatori: The text players read when they win.
goalsDialog.puntiConquistaPerLObiettivo: Conquest points for the completed objective
goalsDialog.laVittoriaArrivaDallEffetto: Victory comes from an event's "Win the adventure" effect (Events tool). The conclusion text and the points below are shown then.
goalsDialog.mettiPrimaIlNemicoIn: First put the enemy on the map with the Enemies tool.
goalsDialog.nemicoConclusioneEPuntiSi: Enemy, conclusion and points can also be written later, but the Check asks for them. Texts are written in markdown:
areaDialog.perEsempioLaSalaDelle: For example: The hall of columns
areaDialog.ilTestoCheCompareA: The text shown on screen when the heroes reveal this area.
areaDialog.laDescrizioneSiScriveIn: The description is written in markdown:
chestsDialog.salvaLeRicompenseSeNe: Save the rewards: if some chest lacks one, the Check will report it
chestsDialog.quandoUnEroeApreUn: When a hero opens a chest they randomly get one of the rewards listed below that matches the quality of the chest opened. You need at least one reward per chest plus any extra ones you want; you can confirm even with an incomplete table, the Check reports what is missing.
encounterDialog.unImmagineDellaRaccoltaD: An image from the token collection or an item's icon in place of the "?". The title is the token's name in the menu and in notifications.
encounterDialog.lEroeSiFermaSulla: The hero stops on the square and picks the action from the "!" menu. Once used, the token disappears from the map: the events "A hero uses an encounter" and "The chosen encounters are no longer on the map" decide the consequences.
eventDialog.ilTestoCheIGiocatori: The text players read (markdown), with the "I've read it" button.
eventDialog.scegliUnOggettoATerra: Choose an item on the ground…
eventDialog.ilNomeDellaChiavePer: The key's name, for example key-1
eventDialog.lIndovinelloOLaSituazione: The riddle or situation the hero reads before rolling (markdown).
eventDialog.ilTestoCheCompareNel: The text shown in the ending, after the adventure's conclusion (markdown).
eventDialog.seCeNEPiu: (if there is more than one, it is enough that one of them happens)
eventDialog.scattaQuandoLUltimoDei: Fires when the last of the chosen enemies (or of all of them, if the list is empty) is no longer on the map or in the area: defeated, removed or walked out. It does not fire if there were none at the start.
eventDialog.scattaQuandoLUltimoDei2: Fires when the last of the chosen encounter tokens (or of all of them, if the list is empty) is no longer on the map or in the area, because it was used. It does not fire if there were none at the start.
eventDialog.soloFincheIlNemicoE: Only while the enemy is inactive
eventDialog.sulNemicoCompareUnE: A "?" appears on the enemy and the adjacent hero finds the same option in the "!" menu. It can be done only once: then the "?" disappears.
eventDialog.scattaAllaFineDelTurno: Fires at the end of the Overlord's turn, after the monsters have played and before the next round begins. Usually used with a condition ("If"), for end-of-turn rewards and penalties.
eventDialog.dopoIlPrimoScattoL: After the first firing the event never starts again, even if another trigger happens. An event whose conditions do not hold does not count as fired.
eventDialog.conUnSoloInnescoL: With a single trigger the event already fires only once. You can choose between "only once" and "every time" when there are several triggers ("or…") or the trigger can repeat, like "a chest is opened in an area".
eventDialog.aggiungiUnaCondizioneSuUna: Add a condition on a variable
eventDialog.aggiungiUnaCondizioneSuUn: Add a condition on an item
eventDialog.siSommaAiValoriChe: It is added to the values it has for the rest of the game (negative to subtract).
eventDialog.esceDallaMappaSenzaBottino: It leaves the map without loot and returns at full health on an already revealed free square, as far away as possible if none is far enough.
eventDialog.seStaAspettandoDiTornare: If it is waiting to come back to life, its defeat is repeated now with the current variables. Otherwise it does nothing.
eventDialog.seIlNemicoEInattivo: If the enemy is inactive (set in Customize), from now on it acts like any other enemy; the stone look, if any, stays. Otherwise it does nothing.
eventDialog.ilNemicoVieneToltoDalla: The enemy is removed from the map without being defeated: no loot and the "defeated" events do not fire.
eventDialog.daOraLeFeriteContano: From now on wounds count: the armor shows its number again. If the enemy is not invincible it does nothing.
eventDialog.ilVecchioStileSvanisceCon: The old look fades out and the new one appears; "Normal" removes the look. The rest (inactive, invincible, immunities) does not change.
eventDialog.mettiPrimaUnOggettoDel: First put a catalog item on the map with the Items tool ("Catalog item" card).
eventDialog.ilGettoneGiaPiazzatoE: The token, already placed and customized on the map, moves to a random free square next to the start squares (not on the start squares). If the event does not fire it stays where you put it. Usually used with "The heroes reveal an area" on the starting area.
eventDialog.lOggettoCompareATerra: The item appears on the ground on a random free square next to the start squares (not on the start squares). Usually used with "The heroes reveal an area" on the starting area. Whoever reaches it picks it up with "Pick up" in the "!" menu.
eventDialog.loRiceveLEroeChe: It goes to the hero who triggered the event. A rune key (or a key) unlocks the doors for the whole party, and the Check counts it for rune doors. An item goes to them (if they have no room, it falls to the ground on their square); money goes to every hero, as in chests.
eventDialog.mettiPrimaUnOstacoloCon: First put an obstacle with the Obstacles tool.
eventDialog.ilVincoloValeDalProssimo: The constraint applies from the Overlord's next turn, both for the script and for whoever plays it. "Normal" removes the behavior.
eventDialog.toglieSoloQuestaVoceLe: It removes only this entry: the enemy's other immunities stay. "All states" does not touch, for example, an immunity to Flame alone that the enemy already had.
eventDialog.lEroeTiraTantiDadi: The hero rolls as many power dice as the extra dice of their chosen attack (with no dice the check fails, unless they buy some with fatigue); the difficulty is the number of waves needed. By default they can spend 1 fatigue for each extra die before rolling; with "No fatigue for the dice" the button does not appear. With "Can be refused" Cancel also appears: nothing happens, the fatigue spent and the interaction cost come back and the "?" stays.
eventDialog.ilSignoreSupremoGuadagnaO: The Overlord gains (or, with a negative number, loses) this Threat; it never goes below 0.
eventDialog.ilSignoreSupremoPescaQueste: The Overlord draws these cards from their deck, as at the start of the turn (if the deck runs out the usual penalty applies); the hand never exceeds the limit.
eventDialog.puntiConquistaFinaliDellObie: Final Conquest points of the objective:
eventDialog.nonFaVincereSePoi: It does not make you win: if the game is won later (for example by defeating the objective's enemy), the ending shows the adventure's conclusion, then this text, and the points are added to those of the objective. Usually used with a condition, for alternative endings.
eventDialog.gliEroiVinconoCompaionoLa: The heroes win: the conclusion and the objective's points appear (written in Objectives), plus the pieces added with "Add to the ending".
behaviorsDialog.regoleCheValgonoPerI: Rules that apply to the monsters of the whole adventure, for the Overlord's script and for whoever plays it. If you choose no monster type they apply to all of them; a single monster can ignore them from Customize.
itemDialog.senzaAspettoIlGettoneE: Without a look the token is the item's icon. The title, if you write one, is the name shown in the "!" menu and in notifications instead of the item's own.
itemDialog.unEroeCheSiFerma: A hero who stops on the square picks it up from the "!" menu. An event ("Move a ground item") can move it next to the start.
monsterDialog.nomeUnMostroConUn: Name (a monster with a name is unique)
monsterDialog.lasciaVuotoPerIlMostro: Leave empty for the card's monster; for example: Narthak
monsterDialog.unMostroConUnNome: A monster with a name cannot be stunned and its name replaces the card's.
monsterDialog.fincheUnEventoNonLo: Until an event activates it, it does not act, is not attacked and has no abilities, but it occupies its squares and blocks movement and sight like an obstacle.
monsterDialog.ogniFeritaCheDovrebbeSubir: Every wound it should take is 0 (hits taken or missed, flame, pits) until an event makes it vulnerable; the armor shield shows ∞. Turning it on adds "All states" to the immunities; turning it off does not remove it.
monsterDialog.soloGraficaAncheSuUn: Graphics only, also on an active enemy. Stone: jagged outline like a boulder, image without color. Crystal: gem-like outline with facets and light reflections.
monsterDialog.mettiPrimaUnOstacoloCon: First put an obstacle with the Obstacles tool.
monsterDialog.unVincoloSuDovePuo: A constraint on where it can stop during the Overlord's turn, the same for the script and for whoever plays it. "Stay put": it never leaves its square. "End the turn next to…": it can move and attack, but always ends next to the chosen obstacle.
monsterDialog.inserisciValoriPositiviONe: Enter values, positive or negative, that modify the monster's normal parameters. Remember that some parameters change with the number of players.
monsterDialog.quelleDellaCartaSiPossono: The card's abilities can be removed with the X (they come back with the + button); the others are added by you.
monsterDialog.aCosaNonESensibile: What it is not sensitive to. "All states" (flame, net, stun, poison) is a separate entry: an event can remove it without deleting the card's immunities.
monsterDialog.quandoMuoreLasciaQuestoGli: When it dies it leaves this. Items fall on its square and, if there are several, on the nearby free squares (or go to whoever deals the fatal blow, if they have room).
variablesDialog.interruttoriConUnNomeTut: Switches with a name (all off at the start): events turn them on and read them to remember what happened, for example "Munkar's heart found".
validator.unknownOne: One unrecognized element (orange placeholder): replace or delete it, otherwise the adventure is not playable
validator.unknownMany: {n} unrecognized elements (orange placeholders): replace or delete them, otherwise the adventure is not playable
validator.stairsOne: A staircase has no partner: place another one to link it, or delete it
validator.stairsMany: {n} staircases do not have two ends: every staircase needs its partner
validator.stairsOkOne: The staircase has both its ends
validator.stairsOkMany: All staircases have both their ends
validator.field.title: title
validator.infoOk: Title, introduction, objective, conclusion and starting Conquest points filled in
validator.goalEventMissing: Victory is left to an event, but no event has the Win the adventure effect
validator.goalGone: The enemy to defeat is no longer on the map
validator.goalInvincible: The enemy to defeat is invincible and no event makes it vulnerable: the adventure cannot be won
validator.goalOk: The enemy to defeat is on the map
validator.behaviorOne: An enemy must end its turn next to an obstacle that no longer exists: choose it again in Customize
validator.behaviorMany: {n} enemies must end their turn next to an obstacle that no longer exists: choose the obstacle again in Customize
validator.encountersOne: An encounter token is not linked to any event
validator.encountersMany: {n} encounter tokens are not linked to any event
validator.encountersOk: All encounter tokens are linked to an event
validator.unassignedOne: A tile does not belong to any area
validator.unassignedMany: {n} tiles do not belong to any area
validator.unassignedOk: Every tile belongs to an area
validator.chestLacking: One or more chests have no reward
validator.areaTextMissing: One or more areas have no description
validator.startGlyphOk: The starting area has the initially lit glyph
validator.startGlyphMissing: The starting area has no initially lit glyph
validator.startCellsOne: The starting area has 1 hero placement square: at least {min} are needed
validator.startCellsFew: The starting area has {n} hero placement squares: at least {min} are needed
validator.startCellsNone: The starting area has no hero placement squares
validator.startCellsOk: The starting area has {n} hero placement squares (at least {min} are needed)
validator.runeMissing: Rune door ({color}): the {color} rune key has not been placed
validator.runeOk: Every rune door has its rune key
validator.eventDoorOne: An event door is not opened by any event: it would stay closed forever
validator.eventDoorMany: {n} event doors are not opened by any event: they would stay closed forever
validator.eventDoorOk: Every event door has an event that opens it
validator.emptyMap: The map is empty: no tile placed
validator.exitsOne: One exit is not closed (no linked tile or dead end). If this is a choice, you can ignore this warning: it does not block the adventure.
validator.exitsMany: {n} exits are not closed (no linked tile or dead end). If this is a choice, you can ignore this warning: it does not block the adventure.
validator.exitsOk: All exits are linked or closed
validator.ev.pieceGone: the enemy is no longer on the map
validator.ev.interactEnemyOnly: you can only interact with an enemy
validator.ev.interactInactive: the interaction is only for inactive enemies, but this one is not: it will never be available
validator.ev.listPieceGone: one of the enemies in the list is no longer on the map
validator.ev.noEnemies: there are no enemies on the map: it will never fire
validator.ev.encounterGone: the encounter token is no longer on the map
validator.ev.listEncounterGone: one of the encounter tokens in the list is no longer on the map
validator.ev.noEncounters: there are no encounter tokens on the map: it will never fire
validator.ev.itemGone: the item is no longer on the map
validator.ev.noChestInArea: there is no chest in the area: the event will never fire
validator.ev.duplicateTrigger: it has two identical triggers: one is enough
validator.ev.varNeverOn: "{name}" is read as on but no event turns it on: the condition will never be true
validator.ev.itemContradiction: the conditions contradict each other on "{name}" (an item is in only one place): it never fires
validator.ev.varContradiction: the conditions contradict each other on "{name}" (on and off at once): it never fires
validator.ev.elseNoCondition: it has effects in "Otherwise" but no condition: they will never fire
validator.ev.thisPieceMisuse: "the event's enemy" can only be used with the "defeated" or "interacts" triggers
validator.ev.targetGone: the enemy to {verb} is no longer on the map
validator.ev.activateNoop: it activates enemies that are not inactive: nothing changes
validator.ev.behaviorObstacleGone: the "next to…" behavior points to an obstacle that no longer exists
validator.ev.finishRevivalNoop: it ends the revival of an enemy that no event brings back to life
validator.ev.moveItemGone: the item to move is no longer on the map
validator.ev.moveItemNoStart: it moves an item next to the start, but there are no start squares
validator.ev.placeItemNoStart: it places an item next to the start, but there are no start squares
validator.ev.checkNoEffects: a check with no effects in either branch: nothing changes
validator.ev.checkAfterCleared: a check after "no enemy left": the active hero rolls it, even if they have nothing to do with what happened
validator.ev.doorGone: the event door to open is no longer on the map
validator.ev.modifyNoop: a change to an enemy changes nothing
validator.ev.reviveNoDefeated: "comes back to life" only applies to a defeated enemy
validator.ev.varOnOff: in "{branch}" the variable "{name}" is on and off at once
validator.ev.multiRevive: in "{branch}" there is more than one "comes back to life"
validator.ev.reviveWin: in "{branch}" "comes back to life" and "win the adventure" contradict each other
validator.ev.winRevive: it can fire together with "{name}", which brings back to life: they contradict each other
validator.ev.winTogether: it can fire together with "{name}" and one of the two wins the adventure: add a condition that tells them apart
editor.missingIntroOne: This adventure contains one element that is missing or not recognized here (for example from a content pack you do not have). You can delete it, or keep it as an orange placeholder: it holds the place and the type and is replaced by putting an element of the same category on top of it. As long as there are any, the adventure counts as not playable in the Check.
editor.missingIntroMany: This adventure contains {n} elements that are missing or not recognized here (for example from a content pack you do not have). You can delete them, or keep them as orange placeholders: they hold the place and the type and are replaced by putting an element of the same category on top of them. As long as there are any, the adventure counts as not playable in the Check.
editor.deleteEventText: The event and everything you wrote inside it will be lost.
editor.deleteAreaText: The subtitle and the description you wrote will be lost. The tiles stay on the map.
editor.importWarning: Everything currently in the editor will be replaced by "{title}". If you have not exported it, it will be lost and this cannot be undone.
editor.saveFailedTitle: Could not save: the browser does not allow it
editor.errLoadingTiles: The editor is still loading the tiles: try again in a moment.
editor.errSave: I can't save the adventure in the browser (storage full or blocked).
editor.errClear: I can't clear the draft in the browser (storage full or blocked).

c.spendi1FaticaPerCurare_bf6af: Spend 1 fatigue to heal 1 wound on yourself. You can use this ability several times, paying its cost each time.
c.esaurisciQuestaCartaPerAnnullare_3dae5: Exhaust this card to cancel 1 wound just received. This card cannot cancel wounds that ignore armor.
c.seiImmuneAlleSeguentiAbilita_2339e: You are immune to the following abilities: Aura, Burn, Knockback, Fear, Grip, Web, Stun and Poison.
c.uccideIlBersaglioAllIstante_2293c: Kills the target instantly, ignoring the immortal ability
c.raddoppiaIlDannoInflittoDa_d741e: Doubles the damage dealt by this attack
c.ricevi50MoneteEPesca_250d7: Receive 50 coins and draw another card from this deck.
c.spendi1PuntoMovimentoE_b96dc: Spend 1 movement point and 1 fatigue token to heal 1 wound on yourself. You can use this ability several times, paying the cost each time.
c.seEEquipaggiatoAllInizio_1582f: If it is equipped at the start of your turn, discard it to recover 6 wounds and your fatigue tokens up to their maximum.
c.quandoSubisci1OPiu_cff9e: When you take 1 or more wounds, roll a power die for each wound taken. Cancel one result for each blank face rolled.
c.esaurisciQuestaCartaPerAnnullare_6f42c: Exhaust this card to cancel 2 wounds just received. This card cannot cancel wounds that ignore armor.
c.laTuaVelocitaBaseE_f5388: Your base speed is reduced to 3
c.quandoEseguiAttacchiMagiciGuadagni_329: When you make magic attacks, you gain a bonus power wave.
c.quandoEseguiAttacchiCorpoA_358b1: When you make melee attacks, you gain +1 damage.
c.duranteIlTuoTurnoDisponi_282d7: During your turn you have 1 more movement point, even if you have none left.
c.seGliHaiInflittoAlmeno_2593d: If you inflicted at least 1 wound on it (after armor is subtracted), place 1 stun token on the target.
c.ricevi50MoneteEUna_4b8f7: Receive 50 coins and a healing potion, then draw another card from this deck.
c.seEEquipaggiatoAllInizio_0903a: If it is equipped at the start of your turn, discard it to recover all hit points and fatigue up to the maximum.
c.spendi1PuntoMovimentoE_ab582: Spend 1 movement point and 1 fatigue token to heal 2 wounds on yourself or on an adjacent model. You can use this ability several times, paying the cost each time.
c.quandoEseguiAttacchiMagiciCon_3a919: When you make magic attacks with this weapon, you gain 2 bonus power waves.
c.seiImmuneAPresaE_b45cb: You are immune to Grip and Daze
c.quandoEseguiAttacchiCorpoA_a58e3: When you make melee attacks with this weapon, you gain 1 bonus power wave.
c.quandoEseguiAttacchiADistanza_ca6a3: When you make ranged attacks, you gain +1 damage and +2 range.
c.esaurisciQuestaCartaPerAnnullare_ba98f: Exhaust this card to cancel 3 wounds just received. This card cannot cancel wounds that ignore armor.
c.scartaQuestaCartaAlTermine_2683f: Discard this card at the end of your turn to place 1 stun token on every monster within 6 spaces of your hero.
c.quandoSubisci1OPiu_c4fee: When you take 1 or more wounds, roll a power die for each wound taken. Cancel 1 wound for each power wave rolled.
c.ricevi150MoneteEUna_d3a8d: Receive 150 coins and a vigor potion, then draw another card from this deck.
c.quandoEseguiAttacchiMagiciGuadagni_11b: When you make magic attacks, you gain +2 range and +2 damage.
c.seiImmuneASanguinareVeleno_88a8c: You are immune to Bleed, Poison and Burn

c.ritmoCostanteAllInizioDel_3b2ff: Steady pace: at the start of their turn they recover 1 fatigue.
c.furiaDelDoloreOgniVolta_f9cef: Pain fury: every time they take wounds from an attack they recover 1 fatigue.
c.ordiniFlessibiliDopoAverRicevuto_353ec: Flexible orders: after getting an order with Prepare, at any time they can spend 2 fatigue to change it for a different one.
c.colpoATradimentoISuoi_372b3: Backstab: their attacks deal +2 damage against an enemy they could not see at the start of the turn.
c.famiglioLoremIpsumDolorSit_1aa5d: Familiar: lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit.
c.nonHaiAbbastanzaFaticaPer_cec15: Not enough fatigue to change order
c.nameStaPerEssereAttaccato_42bd9: {name} is about to be attacked by {name2}. Current order: {order}. Spend {fat:{cost}} to change it?
c.ordineAttualeDiNameOrder_16988: {name}'s current order: {order}. Spend {fat:{cost}} to change it?
c.miraRipetiDeiDadiDel_cc418: Aim: repeat some dice of your next attack, until you move, change equipment or get wounded. Dodge: make an enemy attack be rerolled, until your next turn. Rest: at the start of the next round your fatigue goes back to the maximum, if you are not wounded. Guard: interrupt the Overlord's turn with an attack, until your next turn.
c.dopoAverSceltoDiPrepararsi_ac203: After choosing to **Prepare**, at any time, you may spend 2 fatigue to change the declared order for a different one.
c.allInizioDelTuoTurno_9c9c6: At the start of your turn you recover 1 fatigue.
c.ogniVoltaCheSubisciFerite_9e5e6: Every time you take wounds from an attack you recover 1 fatigue.
c.iTuoiAttacchiInfliggono2_f6de5: Your attacks deal +2 damage against an enemy you could not see at the start of the turn.
c.loremIpsumDolorSitAmet_5a5a3: Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit.
c.quandoSubisciUnaFeritaPuoi_e0fef: When you take a wound, you may reduce it by 1 once per round.
c.spostaNameToccaUnaCasella_aa39e: Move {name}: tap a highlighted square (up to {n} spaces)
c.velocitaSpaziChePercorreOgni_88d91: Speed: spaces it travels each time it moves
c.famiglioNeroIlCorvoE_1a12f: Familiar. Nero the Raven is your familiar: take his token at the start of the game.
c.famigliYingEYangSono_8f4d1: Familiars. Ying and Yang are your familiars: take their tokens at the start of the game.
c.laLineaDiVistaDi_744d0: Francor's line of sight stops the Overlord from summoning creatures, as if he were a hero.
c.volaAttraversaOstacoliAcquaE_65533:
**Flies**: crosses obstacles, water and pits and can stop on any space.

Enemies in Nero's space and in adjacent ones cannot **Dodge** or **Aim** and have 1 less armor.
c.porta1OggettoLoRaccoglie_90d8d: Carries 1 item: it picks it up from the ground and, spending 1 movement point, hands it to a nearby hero or leaves it on the ground.
c.nameLasciaATerraL_37dea: {name} leaves the item on the ground
c.siPortaSenzaUsareLe_b2d7a: Carried without using hands and without taking an item slot.
c.quandoInfliggiAlmeno1Ferita_6b59e: When you deal at least 1 wound with a melee attack, the target gets 1 Burn token.
c.siPuoDareAUn_867fc: It can be given to an adjacent hero (2 movement points) or put down. If its carrier dies it stays on the ground: whoever reaches it takes it.
c.famiglioZannaEIlTuo_bb908: Familiar. Zanna is your familiar: you carry it with you, and you can give it to an adjacent hero by spending 2 movement points. When you deal at least 1 wound with a melee attack, the target gets 1 Burn token.
c.nonSiMuoveDaSolo_fb611: It does not move on its own: a hero carries it, and you can give it to an adjacent hero by spending 2 movement points. When its carrier deals at least 1 wound with a melee attack, the target gets 1 **Burn** token.
